book.title: Little Women
book.author: Louisa May Alcott
book.notes: Spine order: wrap0000 (cover), h-0 (Gutenberg header, title page and table of contents in one document), h-1..h-47 (chapters 1-47). h-1 opens with the heading PART 1 before CHAPTER ONE PLAYING PILGRIMS, so run chapter 1 is titled 'PART 1'; h-24 opens with PART 2 the same way. This key covers run chapters 1-12 only, so it sets partial. Entity types follow Annalist's vocabulary (character, place, organization, artifact, event, concept). The text uses U+2019 apostrophes and curly double quotes; compare names with them folded.

entities.name: Meg March
entities.notes: Eldest sister, sixteen in ch 1. The Moffats call her Daisy (ch 9). Her Pickwick Club name, Samuel Pickwick, the club president, is given in ch 10. 'Miss March' is her formal title as the eldest; see must_not_merge.

entities.name: Jo March
entities.notes: Second sister, fifteen. Aunt March calls her 'Josy-phine'; Mr. Laurence calls her 'Doctor Jo' (ch 5). Pickwick Club name Augustus Snodgrass from ch 10, and she edits the club paper.

entities.name: Beth March
entities.notes: Third sister, thirteen. Pickwick Club name Tracy Tupman from ch 10.

entities.name: Amy March
entities.notes: Youngest sister, twelve. Pickwick Club name Nathaniel Winkle from ch 10.

entities.name: Mrs. March
entities.notes: The girls' mother, mostly called Marmee or Mother. Her forename is not given in ch 1-12.

entities.name: Mr. March
entities.notes: The girls' father, away at the war as an army chaplain. Called Father or Papa from ch 1; the name Mr. March first appears in ch 4. His forename is not given in ch 1-12.

entities.name: Laurie
entities.notes: Mr. Laurence's grandson, the boy next door. Ch 2 knows him only as 'the Laurence boy' and the old man's grandson; ch 3 names him Laurie and Theodore. Pickwick Club name Sam Weller from ch 10. 'Teddy' does not occur in ch 1-12. Never 'Mr. Laurence'; see must_not_merge.

entities.name: Mr. Laurence
entities.notes: Laurie's grandfather, the rich old neighbor. Forename James from the ch 6 letter. 'Mr. Lawrence' is a misspelling in the ch 5 text.

entities.name: Aunt March
entities.notes: Rich, lame, childless old lady; Jo's great-aunt (ch 5) and employer (ch 4). Never called Mrs. March in the text.

entities.name: Uncle March
entities.notes: Dead before the story opens; the library at Aunt March's house was his.

entities.name: Hannah
entities.notes: The Marches' servant since Meg was born. See ambiguities for 'Hannah Brown'.

entities.name: Brooke
entities.notes: Laurie's tutor. Ch 2 mentions 'his tutor' without a name; ch 5 names him. His forename does not occur in ch 1-12.

entities.name: Sallie Gardiner
entities.notes: Meg's friend, of the Gardiner family that gives the New Year's Eve dance (ch 3); surname given in ch 11.

entities.name: Belle Moffat
entities.notes: Annie's engaged elder sister, who dresses Meg up for the party.

entities.name: Mrs. Moffat
entities.notes: Source of the gossip that Mrs. March plans to marry a daughter to Laurie.

entities.name: Mr. Davis
entities.notes: Amy's schoolmaster, who strikes her palm over the limes (ch 7).

entities.name: Pip
entities.notes: Beth's canary; dies of neglect in ch 11 and is buried with an epitaph.

entities.name: The Kings
entities.notes: The rich family whose four children Meg teaches as nursery governess (ch 4). Ch 1 mentions 'the King children'.

entities.name: The Hummels
entities.notes: The poor German family the Marches give their Christmas breakfast to. The mother is never named in ch 1-12.

entities.name: Laurence house
entities.notes: Ch 2 refers to it once as 'the big house next door'; ch 5 describes it and Beth names it the Palace Beautiful. Accept a page from ch 2.

entities.name: Pickwick Club
entities.notes: The sisters' secret society, named for Dickens. Members take Dickens names. Laurie joins in ch 10.

entities.name: The Pickwick Portfolio
entities.notes: The club's weekly newspaper, edited by Jo.

entities.name: Post office
entities.notes: Laurie's post office in the hedge between the two gardens. Not the 'private post office' Mr. Davis suppressed at school (ch 7).

entities.name: Cabinet piano
entities.notes: Mr. Laurence's gift to Beth; it belonged to his dead granddaughter. Not the Marches' old piano (ch 1) nor the Laurences' grand piano (ch 5-6).

entities.name: Jo's book
entities.notes: Half a dozen fairy tales Jo had worked on for years; Amy burns the only copy.

entities.name: Pilgrim's Progress
entities.notes: Bunyan's allegory, which the sisters played as children and now resolve to live by. Not the 'guidebooks' they find under their pillows in ch 2.

entities.name: Camp Laurence
entities.notes: Laurie's picnic for the Vaughns at Longmeadow. The field itself is optional.

optional_entities.name: Longmeadow
optional_entities.notes: The field where Camp Laurence is pitched (ch 12). May be a page of its own or folded into Camp Laurence.

optional_entities.name: Mrs. Gardiner
optional_entities.notes: Hosts the New Year's Eve dance (ch 3).

optional_entities.name: Frank Vaughn
optional_entities.notes: The lame Vaughn twin Beth talks to (ch 12).

optional_entities.name: Grace Vaughn
optional_entities.notes: Youngest Vaughn, Amy's friend at the picnic (ch 12). Not Grace King (ch 4).

optional_entities.name: Mrs. King
optional_entities.notes: Meg's employer (ch 4). The family is the gold entity.

optional_entities.name: Mrs. Hummel
optional_entities.notes: The mother of the Hummels; the text says only 'a poor woman' and 'the Hummels'.

optional_entities.name: Scrabble
optional_entities.notes: Jo's pet rat in the garret (ch 3).

optional_entities.name: John
optional_entities.notes: A Laurence servant who walks Jo home (ch 5). Not Mr. Brooke.

optional_entities.name: The Witches Curse
aliases: The Witches Curse, an Operatic Tragedy
optional_entities.notes: Jo's Christmas play (ch 1-2). Its roles Hugo, Roderigo, Zara, Don Pedro, Hagar and Ferdinando are parts the sisters act, not people.

optional_entities.name: Hugo
optional_entities.notes: Villain of Jo's play, acted by Jo.

optional_entities.name: Mrs. Snowball Pat Paw
optional_entities.notes: The club's lost cat, mourned in the Portfolio (ch 10).

must_not_merge.rule: In narration 'Mr. Laurence' is always the grandfather. Jo calls Laurie 'Mr. Laurence' in ch 3 and he corrects her; Belle Moffat uses it for Laurie in ch 9 and Meg answers as if she meant the grandfather. Keep two pages and never put 'Mr. Laurence' on Laurie's page.

quote.text: “I’m not Mr. Laurence, I’m only Laurie.”

must_not_merge.rule: Every sister is addressed as Miss March: Meg in the ch 3 invitation, Jo by Laurie (ch 3), Beth on Mr. Laurence's letter (ch 6), Amy by Mr. Davis (ch 7). Keep four pages. As the eldest, Meg may carry 'Miss March' as an alias; Jo, Beth and Amy may not.

quote.text: ‘Mrs. Gardiner would be happy to see Miss March and Miss Josephine at a little dance on New Year’s Eve.’

must_not_merge.rule: Both are older March women and both appear from ch 1. 'Mrs. March' in the text is always Marmee; Aunt March is only ever 'Aunt March' or 'Aunt'. Keep two pages.
Mr. March is the living father at the war; Uncle March died before the story (ch 4). Keep two pages and never give Uncle March the name Mr. March.

Pickwick, Mr. Pickwick and Samuel Pickwick are Meg's club name. The Pickwick Club (P.C.) is the organization she presides over. Keep two pages, and never put 'Pickwick' on the club's page as if it were a member.

ambiguities: Miss March: the text uses it for all four sisters. By etiquette it is the eldest's title, so the key lets Meg's page carry it and fails it on Jo's, Beth's or Amy's page. A stricter key would forbid it on every page.

Pickwick Club names (Samuel Pickwick, Augustus Snodgrass, Tracy Tupman, Nathaniel Winkle, Sam Weller) are Dickens characters the sisters and Laurie play in their club. The key models each as an alias of the real person from ch 10, so a separate page for a club name counts as a duplicate page. None of them is a person in the story.
Laurie's first chapter: ch 2 calls him 'the Laurence boy' and the old man's grandson; ch 3 names him. Accept 2 or 3. 'Teddy' does not occur in ch 1-12, so it is not required.

Mr. Brooke: ch 2 mentions Laurie's unnamed 'tutor'; ch 5 names Brooke. The tutor relation is lenient so that an unnamed tutor page from ch 2 merged into Brooke is not marked early. His forename does not occur in ch 1-12, and the 'John' of ch 5 is a Laurence servant.

Laurence house: ch 2 mentions 'the big house next door'; ch 5 describes it and Beth calls it the Palace Beautiful. Gold first_chapter is 5, so a page from ch 2 also passes. Laurie lives_at is lenient for the same reason.

Jo as Aunt March's companion: ch 1 has Jo complain of 'a nervous, fussy old lady' without naming her; ch 4 says it is Aunt March. A link shown in ch 1 or 2 is early. Likewise Meg's governess post: ch 1 has 'teaching those tiresome children' and 'the King children' as separate remarks, and ch 4 joins them.
Aunt March's kinship: 'Aunt March' from ch 1, 'her irascible relative' in ch 4, Jo's 'great-aunt' in ch 5. Lenient.
Uncle March as Aunt March's late husband is implied by his library in her house (ch 4), never stated. Lenient.

Hannah's surname: 'Hannah Brown will preside' in a ch 10 Portfolio advertisement may be a joke name, like 'Mrs. Beth Bouncer' and 'Miss Oranthy Bluggage' in the same column. Do not require it. Katy Brown (ch 7) is an unrelated schoolgirl.
The Christmas guidebooks of ch 2 ('that beautiful old story of the best life ever lived') are not Pilgrim's Progress. Do not record the girls receiving copies of Pilgrim's Progress.

Meg and Laurie: the romance is Moffat gossip in ch 9 ('Mrs. M. has made her plans'), not a fact. Never record laurie suitor_of meg. Mrs. Moffat's 'father a colonel in the army' is also a fib; Mr. March is a chaplain.

Brooke attracted_to Meg (ch 12) is shown, not stated: he looks at her 'a good deal', translates her German song and tutors her in German. A teaching row between them in ch 12 does not satisfy the romance item.

Three pianos: the Marches' old piano (ch 1), the Laurences' grand piano that Beth plays (ch 5-6), and the little cabinet piano Mr. Laurence gives Beth (ch 6), which belonged to his dead granddaughter. Only the last is a gold entity; do not merge them.
Christmas play roles: Jo acts Hugo and Roderigo, Meg acts Hagar and Don Pedro, Amy acts Zara (ch 2). These are parts in a play, not aliases.
Families: the Kings and the Hummels may be modelled as an organization or as a character page for the family. Mrs. King and Mr. King are named in ch 4; the Hummel mother is never named in ch 1-12.

Unnamed dead are not gold entities: Laurie's parents (ch 5), Mr. Laurence's granddaughter (ch 6), Mrs. March's mother (ch 8), and Mrs. March's father, Mr. Laurence's old friend (ch 2 and 5, dead by implication).
'Daisy' is Meg's nickname at the Moffats (ch 9, also spelled 'Daisey'). Jo's 'A regular daisy' in ch 12 is a compliment, not the name.
Pip is a canary typed as a character; if a wiki types him otherwise, his status is not scored.
Camp Laurence is the picnic (event); Longmeadow is the field (optional place). A single page with either name passes only if it carries 'Camp Laurence'.
Mr. Laurence calls Jo 'Doctor Jo' (ch 5) and Beth calls him her 'crochety friend' (ch 6); the girls also call him 'the old gentleman', which the key lists but does not need.
